gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 challenges the identification of the geometric normal space with the Hessian eigenspace and the resulting contraction proof. It does not recognize that the directional bounds and local motion equation fail to characterize the tangent-space distribution or determine when inter-mode probability appears.

ISSUE-010 concerns applying dominant-region derivative bounds over the entire deterministic ridge and the resulting reach estimates. It does not diagnose the early plotted normal-distance stage, the collapse of the tangent-normal eigengap as a_t tends to zero, or the absence of an eigengap reliability check for those measurements.

ISSUE-005 identifies a missing derivative-of-E term in the Newton Jacobian for the stationarity equation. It does not identify the separate estimator defect of accepting a zero normal score without checking the defining negative-curvature condition lambda_{d*+1} <= -beta, so it does not prevent reporting distance to the wrong set.

Both identify the Newton estimator for F(y)=E(y)^T grad log p(y) as invalid because freezing E omits the product-rule contribution (DE)^T grad log p. The prediction also supplies the corresponding full Jacobian and eigengap-dependent repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Hessian-only Newton formula is not the Jacobian of the normal-score equation when the spectral frame varies spatially; the omitted derivative-of-E term prevents the claimed first-order Newton/ridge-distance accuracy.

component_coverage.gold_component: The Newton step for the normal-score equation omits the first-order product-rule term from variation of the eigenvector field, so its claimed accuracy is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that holding E fixed drops (DE[delta])^T grad log p, explains why the Hessian-only formula is not the Newton step, and repairs it with the full product-rule Jacobian and an eigengap condition.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify applying the unrestricted inverse of the selected Hessian block at trajectory points without a nonzero-eigenvalue or conditioning guarantee. The prediction recognizes that the estimator can be undefined or arbitrarily ill-conditioned and gives a safeguarded or damped solve as repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The spectral inverse Lambda_perp(x)^{-1} is used without an input-domain condition ensuring that the selected eigenvalues are bounded away from zero, so the numerical distance step is not well-defined or stable on all admitted inputs.

component_coverage.gold_component: The estimator applies an unprotected inverse of the normal Hessian block at unrestricted inputs, despite no guarantee that its selected eigenvalues are separated from zero.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the spectral inverse is applied at an unrestricted point, explains the resulting undefined or ill-conditioned computation, and proposes a threshold check with Tikhonov damping when needed.
